{
  "tools": [
    {"name": "Meta^n (Meta N)", "url": "https://github.com/minnesotanlp/meta-n"}
  ],
  "on_screen_text": "GitHub - minnesotanlp/meta-n | github.com/minnesotanlp/meta-n | View all files | README | MIT License | Meta^n: Recursive Self-Improvement through Emergent Depth | arXiv 2509.24175 | tests | python 3.11+ | license | Code for the paper Meta^n: Recursive Self-Improvement through Emergent Depth (Zae Myung Kim, Young-Jun Lee, Seungyeon Jwa, Dongyeop Kang, 2026). | Most \"self-improving\" agent loops refine answers, not the process that produces them. Meta^n instead keeps a single universal meta-operation Ω fixed and recurses on its input: Ω reads execution traces from the layers below and writes executable code (a pre_process hook plus a code_library of utilities) that is injected into the layer beneath it, changing its behavior. Applied repeatedly, this produces a stack of self-improving agent layers whose roles emerge from context rather than being prescribed — meta-layers are constructive (they write code) rather than merely evaluative (accept/reject). | How it works | Prior systems either hand-craft a single meta-improvement layer or make one layer edit itself; Meta^n instead stacks the same fixed meta-operation recursively, so depth is bounded by usefulness rather than by design. | (1) Hand-crafted one-layer meta-improvement | (2) Self-referential one layer meta-improvement | (3) Recursive n-layer meta-improvement (ours) | Input Output | Agent | Meta-Layer n | Meta-Layer 3 | Meta-Layer 2 | Layer 1 | Base Solver | Algorithmic Hierarchy, Task router | Genetic mutation, Self-rewrite | Emergent Role or Depth | Validation Score | Faster Convergence & Stronger Generalization | Evolution Iteration | Agentic (Count) | Single-Agent (Ours) | HotpotQA",
  "key_claims": [
    "Meta^n is a research framework/code release for the paper 'Meta^n: Recursive Self-Improvement through Emergent Depth' (arXiv 2509.24175)",
    "Most self-improving agent loops refine final answers rather than the process that produces them, but Meta^n refines the process itself",
    "Meta^n uses a single fixed universal meta-operation that reads execution logs/traces and writes new executable helper code (a pre_process hook plus a code_library) into the layer beneath it",
    "Applying this repeatedly produces a stack of self-improving agent layers whose roles emerge from context rather than being predefined",
    "Meta-layers are constructive (they write code) rather than merely evaluative (accept/reject)",
    "It is a working prototype tested across nine major benchmarks, spanning domains like legal reasoning and terminal commands",
    "The approach yields faster convergence and stronger generalization, improving with every run"
  ],
  "info_channel": "spoken"
}
```
